newsitem.title: UK: UK govt plans bill for stronger competition policy.
newsitem.headline: UK govt plans bill for stronger competition policy.

text.p: The government said on Wednesday it is to bring in a bill to strengthen the deterrents against restrictive agreements and abuses of market power, introducing fines for offenders and third party rights to claim damages.
In her speech opening parliament, written for her by the government, Queen Elizabeth said: "They (the government) will bring forward legislation to reform and strengthen competition law."
Government officials said the bill would introduce a prohibition approach to competition law similar to that contained in the European Union treaty.

"The prohibition regime would provide a much stronger deterrent against restrictive agreements and abuses of market power than is the case under the existing legislation," the officials of the Trade and Industry Department said in a note.
"In particular this would be achieved through the introduction of fines and third party rights for damages and by giving stronger investigatory powewrs to the Director General of Fair Trading."
The new bill will replace the Restrictive Trade Practices Act 1976. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
